scope.flow: cancelWithdrawal then MANAGER_ROLE redelegateWithdrawnHYPE re-delegation via _distributeStake SpotDeposit

statements.text: A user cancels a withdrawal request via cancelWithdrawal, recording the associated HYPE value (totalHypeValueReturned) in _cancelledWithdrawalAmount.
The caller of redelegateWithdrawnHYPE holds MANAGER_ROLE privileges.
_cancelledWithdrawalAmount is nonzero and has a remainder modulo 1e10 when re-delegated.
The MANAGER_ROLE account calls redelegateWithdrawnHYPE, which reads _cancelledWithdrawalAmount, resets it to zero, and re-delegates the amount via _distributeStake with OperationType.SpotDeposit.
_distributeStake calls _convertTo8Decimals(amount, false), computing truncatedAmount = amount / 1e10 with roundUp false.
For SpotDeposit and RebalanceDeposit, the conversion does not account for the remainder amount % 1e10; the remainder is neither added back to hypeBuffer nor included in truncatedAmount sent to L1.
Each redelegateWithdrawnHYPE call loses _cancelledWithdrawalAmount % 1e10 HYPE from the re-delegation process.

The lost HYPE remains in the StakingManager contract outside normal accounting: not recorded in totalStaked, not tracked in hypeBuffer, and not delegated to validators, accumulating as permanently stranded value.
The stranded HYPE reduces protocol capital efficiency and diminishes potential profits for all kHYPE holders.
Re-delegation of cancelled withdrawal amounts should preserve the full HYPE amount, accounting for the amount % 1e10 remainder rather than truncating it outside hypeBuffer and totalStaked.

ambiguities: Report does not state whether the remainder is nonzero in any observed transaction; loss is conditional on _cancelledWithdrawalAmount % 1e10 > 0.
Whether stranded HYPE is recoverable or truly permanent is asserted but not demonstrated.
Exact location of stranded funds (ETH balance vs L1 account) is left uncertain by the report.
